newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Elektrowatt cuts net profit to restructure.
newsitem.headline: Elektrowatt cuts net profit to restructure.

text.p: Swiss building controls and electricity group Elektrowatt AG said provisions for wrapping up a restructuring effort would cut 1995-96 net profit to about 90 million Swiss francs ($71.7 million) from 210 million francs the year before.

Chief executive Oskar Ronner said the group had nearly completed two years of reorganisation into two core areas, buildings and power business, including buying major Swiss security and building control group Landis & Gyr early this year.

"I am convinced that all these radical measures have created the basis for future sales and profit growth that will be above average," Ronner told a news conference on provisional results for the year that ended on Monday (Sept 30).
Ronner said operating profit in 1995-96 should be about 210 million francs, level with the previous year.

Of that, 120 million will go for provisions for loss-making properties held by Swiss unit Goehner Merkur as well as for reducing in-house production at Landis & Gyr Utilities and trimming European business and jobs at unit Elektrowatt Engineering.
Ronner also said Elektrowatt wanted to maintain its dividend at the current percentage.
"Our policy is that we want to maintain the dividend percentage. But the board of directors must make the final decision," he said.

Ronner declined to specify what the dividend payout for the 1995-96 business year would be. The group paid a dividend of 11.50 Swiss francs, or 23 percent of its 50 franc nominal bearer shares, on 1994-95 results.
Elektrowatt, 44.9 percent owned by Swiss financial group CS Holding, also said 1995-96 sales would be around 7.1 billion francs as against 4.98 billion the previous year.

Ronner said previous year figures had not yet been adjusted to reflect the major changes in Elektrowatt's size during 1995-96, including consolidating Landis & Gyr as of last October 1 and divesting Elektrowatt's entire electronics business.

Elektrowatt said its biggest division, building controls and security systens, should post operating profit -- Earnings Before Interest and Taxes or EBIT -- of around 150 million francs in 1995-96 on sales of 4.1 billion. Orders were also around 4.1 billion.
Elektrowatt's power segment, which includes electricity production, distribution and technology, expects a 1995-96 EBIT of around 400 million francs with sales and orders of around three billion.
Ronner declined to comment on prospects of banking group CS Holding selling its 44.9 percent stake in Elektrowatt, which CS Holding has announced it plans to do as part of a strategic refocusing.
"We want to keep Elektrowatt an independent company that is publically traded," he added. ($1=1.2542 Swiss Franc)
